page: Microsoft Azure M96-48bds_2_v3 is a memory-optimized server belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The configuration includes 24 physical cores and 48 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) with hyper-threading enabled. It features a massive memory allocation of 1946.0 GB, which translates to approximately 40.54 GB of RAM per core, and a 105 MB L3 cache. Local storage is bundled, providing 4608 GB of capacity, and the instance is premium storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate strong capabilities across memory and compute tasks. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2205.0 and a multi-core score of 19086.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 67646.12. Memory bandwidth is a notable highlight, reaching 4147.11 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 301.98 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations are highly efficient, with Redis SET operations reaching 66.02 million operations per second. Additionally, the CPU's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 support contribute to strong performance in image processing and LLM prompt processing, where it processed 28.01 tokens per second on a 70B model.

Given the massive memory-to-vCPU ratio and the inclusion of 4.6 TB of local storage, this server represents a high-density resource profile. It is qualitatively cost-effective for workloads that require massive RAM footprints without needing a proportional scaling of compute cores, avoiding the expense of over-provisioning vCPUs. The absence of a dedicated GPU makes it less suitable for heavy GPU-accelerated training, but its high memory bandwidth and capacity make it ideal for large in-memory databases, complex data warehousing, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and heavy virtualization under Microsoft Hyper-V.
